pairs.evidence: src/lib/memory/repo-memory-mirror.ts:154 The scan pipeline these routes run (src/lib/scan.ts calls mirrorRepoMemory) commits untrusted repo-authored `.ai/memory` entries directly into OrgMemory as semantic or procedural rows through a dedup-only door, so an import creates beliefs without the validation the consolidation pass applies.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/memory/scan-feed.ts:97 writeMemoryCandidate's only judgment is same-source duplicate detection before create; the mirror import gets no contradiction or supersedence check against existing items and a fixed confidence of 0.6, rather than being routed through the pass as the technique requires for imports. The grade is at least marked by source and confidence.

src/lib/standard/memory-read.ts:104 A repo-authored convention, which the mirror's own header calls untrusted content, commits as a procedural 'what to do next time' item with no review lane, where third-party material may commit only as an observation about its source. The attribution header and 0.6 confidence mitigate but do not change the lane. The scan-pipeline observation writer in scan-feed.ts does meet the fourth-writer rules (fixed stamp, confidence 1.0, never throws, 0.95 dedup floor).

src/lib/memory/scan-feed.ts:91 The write-time dedup partitions by org, namespace and source before measuring text overlap, and this door only writes shared rows, so similarity cannot cross a scope boundary.
